KV cache and batching interactions with quantized kernels
Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for latency SLOs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45 minutes and go over the quant runs. Samir, you got the agenda?
[00:08] Samir Rao: Yeah thanks Maya, trying to keep this tight, we want to understand quality impact of INT8 and FP8 on our clinical summarization prompts and see if perf gains justify rollout. Jenna from infra is on for the latency and hosting questions.
[00:18] Jenna Brooks: Hey all. Quick note, we care about tail latency at 95th and also about memory usage for Dedicated.
[00:24] Ravi Patel: Great, quick recap from Redwood side: last week we ran INT8 calibration on the 7B variant you gave, used our target-aware quant pipeline, we saw a 2.6x throughput improvement single-stream and about 35% reduction in p95 on hosted on A100s for 2k context. FP8 trials showed similar token quality but slightly better fp8 throughput on Ampere.
[00:44] Tom Hsu: Sorry can you repeat the p95 numbers?
[00:46] Ravi Patel: Yeah so p95 dropped from about 420ms to 270ms at 2k context with INT8 on our hosting cluster. FP8 was about 290ms, tails closer but INT8 seemed best for token throughput.
[01:00] Samir Rao: Ok that looks promising. But quality is king for us — summarization and hallucination are sensitive. What was the delta on rouge/qa?
[01:08] Lina Gomez: We ran the initial 200-case eval you provided. INT8 had a minor drop — roughly 0.9 absolute on ROUGE-L and about 1.2% drop on factual QA exact match versus FP32 baseline. FP8 was within 0.3 on ROUGE-L and less than 0.5% on QA. There were a few outliers where INT8 amplified a wording change that affected clinical meaning; we flagged three examples.
[01:30] Jenna Brooks: Those three examples, do you have diffs? We need to understand if those are model or prompt issues.
[01:36] Lina Gomez: Yes, we'll share the diffs. They look like small tokenization shifts plus lower confidence on rare tokens — could be quantization noise on embedding/kv layers.
[01:44] Maya Chen: Important note, we can try mixed modes: INT8 for most layers and FP16 for first and last N layers to preserve fidelity. That often recovers those edge cases.
[01:53] Samir Rao: Mixed precision sounds ok, but what's the perf hit?
[01:56] Ravi Patel: From our internal runs, mixed-precision gives about 1.8x throughput over FP32, compared to 2.6x for full INT8. So you lose some perf but it's often worth it for quality-sensitive workloads.
[02:08] Tom Hsu: How confident are we in reproducibility across hardware vendors? We run on-prem GPUs sometimes.
[02:12] Ravi Patel: Reproducibility depends on kernel support; our runtime picks kernels per arch. On Ampere and Hopper we've validated both INT8 and FP8 paths, but older gen cards may only do FP16 efficiently. We'll include hardware flags in results.
[02:24] Maya Chen: Also remember KV cache behavior — with quantized weights the cache read/write semantics change a bit and can affect latency for long-context use cases. We saw an extra 15-25ms overhead in some cases when cache hydration hits on INT8.
[02:38] Samir Rao: Hmm that matters for our 8k retrieval flows.
[02:41] Ravi Patel: For 8k, the overall throughput gain still holds, but p95 tail can widen unless you tune batching and prefetch. We recommend prefix caching and proactive batching for high concurrency.
[02:53] Jenna Brooks: On security, last call asked about KMS and audit logs for Private deployment. Any blockers with quantized models?
[02:59] Maya Chen: No link between quantization and KMS. For Private deployments we still support at-rest encryption and HSM-backed keys; audit logs are unchanged. We'll share SOC2 artifacts if needed.
[03:10] Samir Rao: Good. Back to quality: can you run INT8 with mixed FP16 first/last layers and give us diff metrics at 2k and 8k? And include per-example diffs for any clinical critical cases?
[03:20] Ravi Patel: Yes we can. Plan: baseline FP32 at 2k/8k, INT8 full, INT8 mixed (first/last 2 layers FP16), FP8 full. We'll provide ROUGE, QA exact match, and a small hallucination metric we compute.
[03:33] Tom Hsu: For perf, can you do both Hosted numbers and a Dedicated sim? We want to understand Dedicated latency SLOs if we reserve GPUs.
[03:40] Maya Chen: We'll run on hosted infra and also run a Dedicated-shaped workload on a reserved node; note Dedicated can improve p95 due to isolated tenancy but also depends on IO and network egress.
[03:50] Lina Gomez: A note on eval: please send the 1k prompt set with the clinical labels. Our automated eval uses token alignment and QA probes; if you flag critical tokens we can run focused tests.
[03:59] Samir Rao: We'll prepare that and include 50 high-priority cases.
[04:03] Maya Chen: Next on tuning knobs — quantization calibration, per-channel vs per-tensor, clipping thresholds. Ravi, which knobs moved the needle?
[04:10] Ravi Patel: Per-channel calibration for linear layers helped reduce odd token shifts; clipping at 99.9 percentile vs 99.99 had tradeoffs — looser clipping helped perf but increased rare token errors. We suggest per-layer profiles by running a short calibration pass on your in-domain data.
[04:26] Tom Hsu: How long is calibration?
[04:28] Ravi Patel: For 1k samples it's about 20-30 minutes on a single GPU for the model size you're using.
[04:33] Jenna Brooks: Can that run inside our VPC?
[04:35] Maya Chen: Yes for Private deployments or Dedicated we can run calibration in your VPC or on-prem; for Hosted we'll do it in an isolated environment and share artifacts.
[04:44] Samir Rao: What about rollback strategy if quality regressions appear in production?
[04:48] Maya Chen: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks to FP32/FP16 model variants per route. We can set thresholds on QA prompts to auto-roll back.
[04:57] Samir Rao: Good. Any concerns about model drift when quantizing versioned models?
[05:01] Lina Gomez: Versioning matters; we'll store both quantized and baseline variants and run nightly evals. If drift appears on the 1k eval set, we trigger alerts.
[05:10] Ravi Patel: Also note cost math: INT8 reduces memory footprint and allows higher concurrency on the same GPU which lowers per-token cost. We'll include cost estimate delta in the spreadsheet.
[05:19] Tom Hsu: On the examples where INT8 changed clinical wording, do you have suggestions on prompts to mitigate?
[05:23] Lina Gomez: In a couple cases, adding a short system-level constraint to preserve named entities or using constrained decoding helped. We'll include template prompts for your team.
[05:31] Maya Chen: Ok to recap next steps: Redwood runs baseline and mixed-precision tests at 2k/8k, provide perf and quality spreadsheets; Aurelia to share 1k eval and 50 critical cases; schedule Dedicated benchmark session. Action owners are in the notes.
[05:45] Samir Rao: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:48] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the spreadsheet and diffs. Bye.
